Environmental Standards Lookup Table

Source: R/standards.R
standards_tbl.Rd

Default environmental standards used by functions such as [`assign_standards`()].

Format

A tibble with the following columns:

.analyte

Analyte or constituent name.

.standard_type

Standard category or criterion name.

.standard_value

Numeric standard value.

.standard_unit

Unit associated with the standard value.

.location

Optional location identifier for location-specific standards.

.medium

Environmental medium associated with the standard (for example groundwater, soil, sediment, or surface water).

.source

Source authority, regulation, permit, guidance document, or project-specific basis.

.priority

Numeric conflict-resolution priority. Lower values take precedence over higher values.

Details

The dataset is a standardized [`standards_schema`()] object containing regulatory, screening, permit, background, and project-specific environmental standards.

By default, records included with the package represent groundwater screening criteria and drinking water standards. Users may extend or replace this table with custom standards and supply them to [assign_standards()] through the `standards` argument.

Standards are selected according to `.priority`, where lower values indicate higher priority. When multiple standards match a single observation, the standard with the lowest `.priority` value is used.

Standards are stored in a schema-based framework that supports location-specific, medium-specific, permit-specific, and project- specific criteria.

The `.priority` field is used solely to resolve situations where multiple standards apply to the same observation. Lower values represent higher precedence.

Recommended priority ranges are:

  • 1-9 = Site- or project-specific objectives

  • 10-19 = Permit limits and compliance criteria

  • 20-49 = Regulatory standards

  • 50-99 = Screening levels and guidance values

  • 100+ = Background, reference, or informational values

These ranges are recommendations only. Users may define any priority system appropriate for their project provided that lower values represent higher precedence.

Examples

data("standards_tbl", package = "manager")

standards_tbl
#> # A tibble: 15 × 12
#>    .analyte      .standard_type .standard_value .standard_unit .location .medium
#>    <chr>         <chr>                    <dbl> <chr>          <chr>     <chr>  
#>  1 Antimony      Maximum Conta…               6 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  2 Arsenic       Maximum Conta…              10 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  3 Barium        Maximum Conta…            2000 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  4 Beryllium     Maximum Conta…               4 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  5 Cadmium       Maximum Conta…               5 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  6 Chromium      Maximum Conta…             100 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  7 Cobalt        Regional Scre…               6 ug/L           NA        ground…
#>  8 Fluoride      Maximum Conta…               4 mg/L           NA        ground…
#>  9 Lead          Regional Scre…              15 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 10 Lithium       Regional Scre…              40 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 11 Mercury       Maximum Conta…               2 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 12 Molybdenum    Regional Scre…             100 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 13 Selenium      Maximum Conta…              50 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 14 Thallium      Maximum Conta…               2 ug/L           NA        ground…
#> 15 Radium-226 a… Maximum Conta…               5 pCi/L          NA        ground…
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: .source <chr>, .provenance <chr>, .reference <chr>,
#> #   .effective_date <date>, .notes <chr>, .priority <int>

# Add a custom site-specific standard
custom_standards <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  standards_tbl,
  tibble::tibble(
    .analyte = "Arsenic",
    .standard_type = "Site Cleanup Standard",
    .standard_value = 5,
    .standard_unit = "ug/L",
    .location = "MW-01",
    .medium = "groundwater",
    .source = "Project",
    .priority = 1L
  )
)
